court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent were married in 2020. A child was born out of wedlock. Respondent filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights. Petitioner is unable to contest the case from Chennai.

legal_principles.principle: The domicile or citizenship of the opposite party is immaterial in a case like this.
legal_principles.held: In case the marriage was solemnized under Hindu Law marital relationship is governed by the provisions of the Hindu Marriage Act. Therefore, Section 19 has to be given a purposeful interpretation.

legal_principles.principle: The objects and reasons which prompted the parliament to incorporate a provision have also to be taken note of.
legal_principles.held: Sub Clause (iii-a) was inserted in Section 19 with a specific purpose. Experience is the best teacher.

legal_principles.principle: Where the petitioner's wife has pleaded lack of money, the same has to be considered.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that where the petitioner's wife has pleaded lack of money, the same has to be considered.
cited_cases: Geeta Heera vs. Harish Chander Heera [(2000) 10 SCC 304]

legal_principles.principle: The place of residence of the wife determines the question of jurisdiction.
legal_principles.held: The Supreme Court has allowed the transfer petition considering the distance and the difficulties faced by the wife.
cited_cases: Lalita A.Ranga vs. Ajay Champalal Ranga [(2000) 9 SCC 355]

outcome.final_order: Petition for transfer allowed, HMOP No. 281 of 2021 withdrawn from Sub Court, Devakottai and transferred to Family Court at Chennai.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for transfer to family court
advising on restitution of conjugal rights
assisting with divorce proceedings under Hindu Marriage Act
